parsed.title: fold-findings still routes REPLAN straight to /execute-phase
parsed.detail: The unit's own AC7 requires 'no converged surface sends a replan row to the executor or the fold', and fold-findings/SKILL.md is one of the eight converged surfaces — yet its per-finding report contract still prints `REPLAN <proposed phase(s) → /execute-phase>` and its Done-when closing block still says `· any REPLAN (<F1> + <F2> + …) → confirm all proposed SPEC phases, then /execute-phase on this same branch`. Both contradict the new canonical destination the same file's freeze-batch section and branch table now state (router → planner → fresh /review-plan → execute-phase). The exact 'two contradictory sentences' defect class the fix claims to remove survives inside a converged surface.

parsed.title: router-first gate BLOCKs the planners' primary paths
parsed.detail: ROUTING.md now orders 'Before the status gate, run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN>`' and only says 'a router that cannot run is BLOCKED' — but the router exits 1 ('unknown unit') for any slug with no unit folder (unit-route.mjs `fail(1, "unknown unit: …")` when `matches.length === 0` and the token is non-numeric). A brand-new feature slug (ROUTING step 5: 'Roadmap row status `idea`, or no row at all → STOP → /design-feature') and a brand-new fix issue not yet in the fix index (plan-fix's core input, per PLANNING_PROCESS 'run the router before ingest') both produce exit 1, which is neither 'any other route' nor 'cannot run' — leaving the documented undesigned-feature redirect and new-issue drafting paths blocked. Exit 1 is a determined answer, not a missing script.

parsed.title: preflight mandatory vs skipped on the replan route
parsed.detail: Progressive-loading item 2 says 'Any route that can write planning artifacts: … consume the planning preflight … before composing an internal step', and appending SPEC phases is a planning-artifact write. Item 4 plus skills/replan-findings/SKILL.md ('**No planning preflight.** … the normalized-repository-state read `planning-preflight` owns is not consumed on this route') contradict item 2 within the same allowlist — one of the two rules must be false.

parsed.title: `rows:` line lists all open rows, not the route-selected ones
parsed.detail: `const rowIds = rows.map((row) => row.id)` prints every open row: for fixture 10-replan-unit the test itself asserts `rows: F1 F2 F3` where only F2 is replan-routed (F1=fold, F3=decision). But replan-findings/SKILL.md says 'The `rows:` line names the findings … Read exactly those rows' and PHASE_APPEND.md says 'For every finding the router's `rows:` line selected, append one or more phases' — a consumer following the contract appends phases for the fold/decision rows too, violating the contract's own 'Never widen the scope past the selected rows' guardrail. AC5 passes only because unit 37's open rows happen to be all-replan.

parsed.title: freeze-batch claims `route: replan` for decision-required rows
parsed.detail: The freeze-batch condition is '≥ 1 row with frozen class `replan-in-unit` **or `decision-required`**', and the new text says the loop 'routes to `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`, whose `route: replan` line names the planner'. For a decision-required row the router prints `route: decision` with `next: decision required — stop and surface to the user` (unit-route.mjs DECISION_ROUTE branch) — no replan line and no planner. The fold's documented consumer action is unactionable for half its own trigger set.

parsed.title: sensor routes decision-required rows to the fold, router says decision
parsed.detail: `readSuggestions` only tests PLAN_ROUTE; a `decision-required` open row falls into the `rows.length > 0` branch and emits `{command: "/fold-findings"}`. The router the changelog says 'owns the class→destination decision' answers `route: decision` for the same row (fixture 12-decision-unit), and normative-drift's new test claims 'neither may invent a fourth destination for the same class' — here the two machine surfaces disagree on the decision class's destination.

parsed.title: new skill missing from the plugin manifest
parsed.detail: The skills array enumerates every workflow skill including internal ones (`./skills/implementation-discovery`, `./skills/evidence-grounding`, …) but has no `./skills/replan-findings` entry. AC9's 'the new internal skill is registered … the skill tree stays discoverable' and SKILLS.md's registration claim are not satisfied on the plugin-manifest discovery surface this file owns.

parsed.title: stray `|---|` appended to new changelog rows
parsed.detail: Every added row in this unit ends with a literal `|---|` inside the last cell (e.g. `…publish the re-bundle. |---|`, also on the 3.5.0, 5.2.0, 3.2.0, 3.5.1, 1.5.0 and 2.8.0 rows and their ES siblings). That renders as literal text in the table cell — a markdown defect in the release record repeated across both CHANGELOG files.

parsed.title: double negative in the 3.5.0 cell
parsed.detail: 'a plain fix-now row to `/fold-findings`, no open row contributes nothing' literally asserts every open row contributes something; the intended claim (per AC6: 'a unit with no open row contributes no suggestion') is the opposite. The ES sibling repeats it ('ninguna fila abierta no aporta nada').

parsed.title: step 4 drops the fresh /review-plan its own step 3 just added
parsed.detail: Step 3 now requires 'the fresh `/review-plan <unit>` that must pass before execution', but step 4 still says 'After a replan, ask the user to continue manually with `/execute-phase <unit> P<n>`' with no review-plan step — the same file contradicts itself about whether execution may follow the replan directly.

parsed.title: stale 'Both resources' after the allowlist grew
parsed.detail: The closing line of the progressive-loading section still reads 'Do not load planning gates after a redirect stop. Both resources are normative, one hop from this file' — the allowlist it closes now has four entries, so 'Both' no longer refers to anything countable.
